findings.title: Removal of findMany breaks existing callers
findings.body: The previous public method findMany(findManyArgs) was removed and replaced with getBaseConditions(). Only the service and its integration tests are updated in this PR, so any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService.findMany() will fail TypeScript compilation or, if untyped, throw at runtime. If the raw-SQL conversion is intentional, the same PR should either migrate all call sites or keep a findMany wrapper that builds a raw query from getBaseConditions().

findings.title: Org authorization omits user bookings when org has no child teams
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only queries userIdsFromOrg when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. An organization can have accepted members via the org membership itself even when it has no child teams, but in that case the isTeamBooking = false branch is omitted entirely. As a result, an org owner/admin cannot see personal/user-scoped bookings of org members for organizations without child teams. The guard should not depend on teamsFromOrg.length, or the membership query should still run with [options.orgId].

findings.title: Public options type makes invalid team scope calls compile
findings.body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions declares teamId optional for every scope, whereas the zod schema still requires teamId when scope is 'team'. This means new InsightsBookingService({ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }) now compiles, then safeParse fails in the constructor and the service silently returns NOTHING_CONDITION. This moves a real configuration error from compile time to runtime. The public type should remain a discriminated union or otherwise require teamId for scope 'team'.

findings.title: Org/team raw SQL branches are never executed against the database
findings.body: The team and org authorization tests only assert that the generated Prisma.sql object equals an expected Prisma.sql object. They do not run a query using those conditions, so a SQL syntax error, invalid ANY(array) parameter binding, or incorrect column/table mapping in the org/team OR branches would not be caught. The only end-to-end query test uses user scope. Consider adding a $queryRaw execution for at least one team or org branch where the generated SQL is actually sent to the database.
